newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money steady, new gilt active.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money steady, new gilt active.

text.p: Indian call money was quoted around 5.75 percent in morning trade on Friday, against the opening quotes of 5.5-6.0 percent, dealers said.
"Demand has dropped off a bit from the opening," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Call rates should ease off to around 5.0-5.5 percent by close of trade."

Dealers said the latest security issued by the government of India was active on Friday. The Reserve Bank of India auctioned 10 billion rupees of 10-year bonds on Thursday at a yield of 13.65 percent, down from earlier issues of 13.85 percent.
"The new stock is being actively traded at a premium," said a dealer. "Trades have already been struck at 31 paise over the issue price of 100 rupees."
"There are also a lot of quotes in other securities maturing in 2005 and 2006 but little trade so far," he added.
